name: Kenosha Unified School District
calendarType: Four coordinated instructional calendars: boundary elementary, boundary middle, boundary high, and Frank Elementary alternate calendar
seoTitle: Kenosha Unified School District Calendar: KUSD Dates & PDFs
seoDescription: Reviewed KUSD calendar dates for elementary, middle and high schools, plus Frank Elementary's alternate year, conferences, Friday releases, breaks and official PDFs.
districtFact: KUSD serves the City of Kenosha, Village of Pleasant Prairie, and Town and Village of Somers. Its calendar is not one uniform sheet: boundary elementary, middle, and high schools have separate PDFs, while Frank Elementary follows an alternate calendar that starts in early August.

about.title: Three PDFs Make the Boundary-School Calendar
about.content: KUSD publishes separate elementary, middle, and high school PDFs. Shared holidays and staff days align, but conferences, Friday release patterns, high school exams, assessments, and the graduating-senior last day differ by level. No single one of those PDFs represents every KUSD student.

about.title: Frank Elementary Uses an Alternate Year
about.content: Frank K-5 students begin August 3 and Frank 4K begins August 10—weeks before the September boundary-school opening. Frank then uses Enrichment Weeks and its own conference, professional-learning, workday, and closure dates, so Frank families should use the dedicated PDF rather than the boundary elementary calendar.

about.title: Friday Means Different Things by Grade Band
about.content: The boundary elementary and Frank PDFs mark regular Fridays as early-release days. Boundary middle and high schools generally keep full Fridays, except specified half days or high school final-exam releases. This recurring rule matters more than a generic districtwide bell-time assumption.

about.title: LakeView K-8 and Ruth Harman Follow Middle-School Conferences
about.content: KUSD's year page excludes LakeView K-8 and Ruth Harman from boundary-elementary conference closures and groups them with middle-school evening conferences. Families at those schools should not copy the elementary October or February no-school dates without checking their assigned schedule.

about.title: Four Quarters Share One Common Backbone
about.content: The three boundary calendars use the same quarter endpoints, staff workdays, professional-learning days, Thanksgiving, Winter Break, Spring Break, and final student half day. The grade-band PDFs then add their own conference and testing layers.

about.title: KUSD Covers Four Kenosha-Area Municipalities
about.content: Created in 1967, KUSD includes Kenosha, Pleasant Prairie, and both the Town and Village of Somers. The district reports 16 elementary schools, four middle schools, three high schools, six choice schools, one specialty school, and one Head Start center.

calendarNotes: KUSD's public schedule is a coordinated set of grade-band calendars rather than a single district PDF. The boundary elementary calendar carries Friday early release and elementary conference closures. The middle calendar controls Bullen, Lance, Mahone, and Washington conference dates and also provides the conference pattern used for LakeView K-8 and Ruth Harman. The high school calendar adds evening conferences, final-exam early releases, ACT and PreACT attendance splits, and a separate last day for graduating seniors. Frank Elementary begins in August and alternates instructional blocks with Enrichment Weeks. Shared red closure dates and gold professional-learning dates align across the calendars, but a school-specific label must not be interpreted as a districtwide closure. Families should use the student's school and grade band before importing any date.

planningTips.title: Planning with the KUSD Calendar Set
content: Choose the student's calendar first: boundary elementary, boundary middle, boundary high, or Frank Elementary alternate calendar.
Treat Friday early release as a recurring elementary and Frank rule; middle and high school Fridays are not automatically shortened.
For LakeView K-8 or Ruth Harman, use the middle-school conference dates named by KUSD instead of the boundary-elementary conference closures.
Keep the September 1 K-12 start separate from the September 8 boundary 4K start and Frank's August 3 K-5 / August 10 4K opening.
On ACT and PreACT dates, verify the student's grade: tested grades attend for assessment and early release while other high school grades do not report.
Use the dedicated Frank PDF for Enrichment Weeks; those blocks are not school breaks for the rest of KUSD.
For weather, check KUSD alerts before 5 a.m.; a two-hour delay cancels both morning and afternoon early childhood, speech impact, and 4K classes.

livingHere.intro: KUSD's boundary and choice-school structure spans the Kenosha lakefront, Pleasant Prairie, and Somers, with start times and instructional calendars that vary by school design.

highlights.label: 18,719 students
highlights.detail: KUSD reports 8,645 students in 4K-grade 5, 3,981 in grades 6-8, and 6,093 in grades 9-12.

highlights.label: 31 schools and centers
highlights.detail: The published count combines 16 elementary, four middle, three high, six choice, one specialty, and one Head Start site.

highlights.label: Boundary and choice options
highlights.detail: Students receive a boundary assignment by address, while families may apply annually to KUSD choice schools.

highlights.label: Several daily schedules
highlights.detail: Elementary campuses use multiple start-time groups, while middle, high, K-8, and choice schools publish their own hours.

highlights.label: Frank alternate calendar
highlights.detail: Frank Elementary is the district's clearly published early-start track, with August opening and Enrichment Weeks.

highlights.label: Weather operations
highlights.detail: KUSD may open normally, open two hours late, or close all schools; a closure also cancels after-school sports, fine arts, and evening events.

districtFaqs.q: Does KUSD have one calendar for every school?
districtFaqs.a: No. KUSD publishes separate boundary elementary, middle, and high school calendars, plus an alternate calendar for Frank Elementary. Shared closures align, but conferences, releases, tests, and some school dates differ.

districtFaqs.q: When do KUSD students start school?
districtFaqs.a: Boundary-school K-12 students start September 1 in both reviewed years, and boundary 4K starts September 8. Frank Elementary K-5 starts August 3 and Frank 4K starts August 10.

districtFaqs.q: Do all KUSD elementary students leave early on Fridays?
districtFaqs.a: The official boundary elementary and Frank PDFs mark Fridays as early-release days. Families should use their school's published hours because dismissal time varies by campus.

districtFaqs.q: Which conference calendar applies to LakeView K-8 and Ruth Harman?
districtFaqs.a: KUSD groups LakeView K-8 and Ruth Harman with the middle-school evening conference schedule and excludes them from the boundary-elementary conference release and no-school dates.

districtFaqs.q: What are Frank Elementary Enrichment Weeks?
districtFaqs.a: They are blocks on Frank's alternate instructional calendar, not districtwide breaks. The dedicated Frank PDF distinguishes Enrichment Weeks from red dates when Frank is closed.

districtFaqs.q: What happens when KUSD opens two hours late?
districtFaqs.a: KUSD states that morning and afternoon early childhood, speech impact, and 4K classes are canceled on a two-hour-delay day. Other schools open two hours late.

districtFaqs.q: Does a KUSD weather closure cancel evening activities?
districtFaqs.a: Yes. KUSD says a building closure also cancels after-school activities, including sports, fine arts, and evening events.

customSections.label: Which KUSD Calendar Should You Use?
customSections.content: The school assignment—not just the student's grade—determines the correct calendar.

customSections.label: KUSD Weather Decisions Change More Than the Start Time
customSections.content: KUSD announces emergency changes through district text alerts, its website, Channel 20, social media, and local media, generally by 5 a.m. A two-hour delay cancels early childhood, speech impact, and 4K sessions; a full closure also cancels after-school and evening activities.
